overall_quality.evidence: Object-oriented programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm that uses objects and their interactions to design applications and computer programs. The principles of OOP include encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism. Encapsulation involves bundling data and methods that operate on the data into a single unit called an object. Inheritance allows objects to inherit properties and methods from other objects, promoting code reuse. Polymorphism enables objects to take on multiple forms, allowing for more flexible and reusable code.
